llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requested environment variable line up with its stated purpose (upload a single local file to the vendor's OSS and call Duhui's async convert API), though it does upload user files to vendor-controlled storage which is a privacy consideration.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required binary (python3), and required env var (DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE) match the included script and references. The script implements the described flow (fetch temporary OSS credentials, upload to vendor OSS, call convert_async, poll, download PDF). No unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and script explicitly instruct the agent to upload the local source file to a vendor-controlled OSS bucket and to fetch temporary upload credentials from a vendor URL. This is coherent with the service but means user files are transmitted to the vendor; the doc calls this out and attempts best-effort cleanup. The instructions avoid echoing AppCode and restrict inputs (no direct URLs/Base64), which is appropriate.

dimensions.detail: Only DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE is required and is justified for calling the Alibaba Market API. The script also fetches temporary OSS credentials at runtime from a vendor endpoint (expected for this upload flow) and does not request unrelated secrets or system config paths.

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not modify other skills or system settings. The script caches temporary OSS credentials in memory only and documents that it will not persist AppCode; it performs best-effort remote cleanup but does not claim persistent privileged presence.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it uploads a single local file to the vendor's temporary OSS bucket, calls Duhui's async convert API with your DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE, polls for completion, downloads the PDF, and attempts to delete the temporary object. Before installing/using it, consider: (1) privacy — your local file will be uploaded to vendor-controlled storage (fmtmp.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com) and may remain there briefly if deletion fails; only use with files you are comfortable sharing with the vendor; (2) AppCode handling — ensure your agent injects DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE securely and does not log or echo it; (3) trust the vendor endpoint that provides temporary OSS credentials (https://file.duhuitech.com/k/tmp_up.json) since the script uses those creds to upload files; (4) if you need offline conversion or cannot share files externally, use a local converter (LibreOffice/unoconv) instead. If you want higher assurance, review/run the included script in a sandboxed environment and inspect network calls during a test run.
